chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade playing with chess and backgammon (dice).
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on playing chess and backgammon according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records a prohibition by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) regarding the game of chess (ash-shatranj) and backgammon/dice (an-nard). It serves as a primary textual basis in Shia jurisprudence for the ruling on these specific games, with scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid and Al-Sharif al-Murtada discussing whether the prohibition is due to distraction from prayer or the element of gambling inherent in their play. The chain of narration highlights the transmission of this ruling through prominent early scholars, reinforcing its authenticity in Usul al-Kafi.
